name: Decline Dumbbell Squeeze Press
description: A decline bench pressing variation where both dumbbells are pressed together throughout the entire movement, creating a constant adduction force that maximally activates the medial and sternal fibers of the pectoralis major. The decline angle combines with the continuous squeeze to target the lower chest with both pressing and adduction force simultaneously.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a decline bench with feet secured. Hold two dumbbells pressed firmly together above the lower chest with palms facing each other. Arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the bench to a 15–30 degree decline. Use hexagonal dumbbells as their flat sides make maintaining contact easier.
steps: Step 1: Begin with dumbbells pressed together above the lower chest, palms facing each other. Maintain active squeezing pressure throughout.
Step 2: Lower the dumbbells as a single unit toward the lower chest, keeping them in constant contact.
Step 3: Descend until the dumbbells are at chest level.
Step 4: Press the unit back up to the starting position, squeezing the dumbbells together the entire time.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on the press back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the dumbbells separate during the movement — the squeeze must be continuous
Using dumbbells too heavy to maintain the squeeze while pressing
safety_considerations: Secure feet firmly on the decline to avoid sliding
Get a spotter to hand you the dumbbells in position to avoid awkward setup
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from chest to full arm extension. The adduction force is maintained throughout.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-1-2-1 (3s descent, 1s pause, 2s press, 1s squeeze at top)
coaching_cues: Squeeze the dumbbells together as hard as possible the entire set
Press from the inside out — the squeeze generates the tension
